one_liner: PHP's built-in opcache JIT: 2-9.5x faster than the plain PHP 8.2 interpreter on numeric benchmarks-game kernels.
what_it_does: The JIT is part of the opcache extension in php-src: it compiles PHP opcodes to native x86, x86-64 or AArch64 code at run time, either whole functions (opcache.jit=function) or hot traces (opcache.jit=tracing). There is no API; existing PHP code runs unchanged once opcache is enabled and a JIT mode and jit_buffer_size are set in php.ini or with -d flags. Since PHP 8.4 the back end is the embedded IR framework (dstogov/ir); the 8.2.3 build that was benchmarked used the older DynASM back end (zend_jit_x86.dasc, zend_jit_arm64.dasc).
how_it_is_fast: The tracing mode (opcache.jit=1255 in the benchmark: AVX allowed, global linear-scan register allocation, hot-trace trigger, type inference plus inter-procedural analysis) records hot loops and functions after hot counters fire, specialises them on observed types and emits native code, so loops on ints and floats skip the VM's opcode dispatch and zval type checks. Since 8.4 the code is generated through IR, a Sea-of-Nodes style SSA graph modelled on LuaJIT's IR, with on-the-fly folding, SCCP, global code motion and linear-scan register allocation. Calls into C code (PCRE, GMP, string functions) are not sped up, which is why regex, string and bignum kernels barely move.
when_to_use: CPU-bound PHP loops on ints and floats (math, image and pixel loops, emulators, simulations): the independent run shows mandelbrot 9.5x, fannkuchredux 3.3x, nbody 3.1x and spectralnorm 2.6x over the no-opcache interpreter (ratios derived from page data).
Long-running PHP CLI workers or daemons, where trace compilation is paid once and the best-iteration numbers above apply.
Existing PHP 8.x deployments on x86-64 or AArch64 that cannot change runtime or language: it is enabled with ini settings only.
Object- and allocation-heavy PHP code such as tree building, where binarytrees still ran 2.0x faster (2.93 s vs 5.84 s).
when_not_to_use: Typical request-per-process web apps bound by database and network I/O (WordPress-style): the PHP JIT RFC reports large gains only on bench.php and Mandelbrot and little for real apps (RFC page blocked here, search snippet only).
Code whose time is in C extensions: regexdna (PCRE) 1.39 s vs 1.40 s, pidigits (GMP) 1.57 s vs 1.71 s and revcomp 2.06 s vs 2.27 s were essentially unchanged.

When you need LuaJIT-, PyPy- or V8-class speed: on the same page PHP JIT is behind LuaJIT on spectralnorm (2.51 s vs 0.12 s) and nbody (7.0 s vs 1.44 s) and behind PyPy3 on spectralnorm (2.51 s vs 0.71 s) and nbody (7.0 s vs 4.44 s).
Architectures other than i386, x86-64 and AArch64: configure disables the JIT with a warning; on Apple Silicon a ZTS build needs pthread_jit_write_protect_np().
Risk-averse production code on PHP 8.4-8.6 without testing: several verified JIT miscompilation bugs are open (see gotchas).

integration.dependencies: none beyond PHP itself; the IR framework is embedded in ext/opcache/jit/ir; Capstone is optional, only for JIT disassembly
integration.min_toolchain: PHP 8.0 or later (JIT introduced in 8.0; IR-based back end from 8.4); built with PHP's normal C toolchain, no extra compiler requirement documented in what was read
integration.platforms: i386, x86-64 and AArch64 per the JIT README and config.m4 (which has Linux/BSD and macOS targets; the Windows build files were not checked); other CPUs run the interpreter
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the files read; config.m4 only notes that ZTS builds on Apple Silicon require pthread_jit_write_protect_np()
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: drop-in for the PHP interpreter (same code, ini switch), but not a replacement for the category's baselines (PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot), which run other languages

gotchas: Harness: kostya/jit-benchmarks runs each program up to 5 times inside one process and reports the fastest self-timed (microtime) iteration, so start-up and first-pass JIT compilation are excluded; knucleotide, regexdna and revcomp ran a single iteration, and the no-JIT nbody hit the 80 s timeout after 3 iterations. The PHP knucleotide program fails the suite's own output check (tools/benchmarks.rb lists php and php_jit under expected_check_failed): its do ... while ($i) loop never counts position 0 and divides by strlen - k. Both PHP rows ran that same code, so the JIT ratio stands, but the cross-language knucleotide row is unvalidated. The README header says PHP8.1 while the versions table says 8.2.3, and there are no PHP rows for brainfuck, brainfuck2 or matmul.

The baseline row loads no opcache at all, so the speedup includes opcache's optimizer passes as well as the JIT; and the measured 8.2.3 JIT is the DynASM back end that PHP 8.4 replaced with the IR framework, so the numbers do not transfer directly to current releases.

Open, maintainer-verified miscompilations: #22559 (tracing JIT in 8.4-8.6, not 8.3: high bits of ~ leak through a masked OR into a typed int property, 0x9C became 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF in a Z80 emulator), #23983 (function JIT in 8.4+: wrong boolean result when interrupt handlers run inside a loop, fix PR #24003) and #23572 (tracing JIT calls the wrong method for self::/parent:: static calls in shared trait methods).

Configuration traps: since 8.4 the defaults are opcache.jit=disable and opcache.jit_buffer_size=64M, so setting only jit_buffer_size no longer enables the JIT, and JIT start-up failures are fatal; since 8.5 opcache is always built in and zend_extension=opcache.so (as in the benchmark's command line) emits a warning; the CLI needs opcache.enable_cli=1.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Like the CPython copy-and-patch JIT and BeamAsm siblings, this is a JIT measured against its own runtime's interpreter; it is the only option for unmodified PHP code and shows much larger numeric gains (2-9.5x) than CPython's JIT (7-8% geomean), while the HHVM sibling's 1.6x over PHP comes from a 2014-era comparison. If you want to build your own JIT in C, look at the IR framework that PHP 8.4+ embeds rather than at php-src.
verified_claims_summary: kostya/jit-benchmarks round 1 (2023-02-28) built PHP 8.2.3 from source (configure defaults, gcc 12.2.0, Ubuntu 22.10 in Docker on a Ryzen 7 3800X) and ran the same PHP programs with the tracing JIT (opcache.jit=1255, 500M buffer) and without opcache: best iteration times mandelbrot 0.58 vs 5.51 s, fannkuchredux 0.77 vs 2.54 s, nbody 7.0 vs 21.77 s, spectralnorm 2.51 vs 6.48 s, binarytrees 2.93 vs 5.84 s and fasta 2.46 vs 4.64 s, while regexdna, pidigits and revcomp stayed within 10%.
status_note: Actively developed in php-src (40.4k stars, commits on 2026-10-06, master BSD-3-Clause, the tested 8.2.3 under the PHP License 3.01) and shipped with every PHP 8 build but off by default; it is usable only as part of the PHP runtime, and the reusable piece for other projects is the IR framework (github.com/dstogov/ir), which its README says is still under development.
